sentences: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) is typically treated with a combination of antibiotics and supportive care
The primary goal of treatment is to eliminate the infection, alleviate symptoms, and prevent long-term complications
The choice of antibiotics depends on the severity of the infection, the patient's medical history, and any allergies or sensitivities
For mild to moderate PID, a combination of oral antibiotics such as ceftriaxone and doxycycline is often prescribed
For more severe cases, hospitalization may be necessary, and intravenous antibiotics such as cefotetan and clindamycin may be administered
In addition to antibiotics, supportive care is essential in managing PID symptoms
Pain management with over-the-counter pain relievers such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen
Rest and hydration to help the body recover from the infection
Avoiding sexual activity until symptoms resolve and the patient is no longer contagious
Follow-up appointments with a healthcare provider to monitor progress and adjust treatment as needed
In some cases, surgical intervention may be necessary to treat complications of PID, such as tubo-ovarian abscesses or infertility
A healthcare provider will determine the need for surgery on a case-by-case basis
